cards.explanation: The answer is an alabaster jar of perfume. The text says she learned Jesus was dining there and brought an alabaster jar of perfume (Luke 7:37). Remember that jar, friends, because it's about to matter. Me, I'd have walked in with a box of cookies and been WAY too proud of myself.
The answer is True. She began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair (Luke 7:38). No towel is mentioned, just her hair. I think she gave Him what she had right there with her.
The answer is that she anoints His feet with it. She kissed His feet and then anointed them with the perfume (Luke 7:38). Feet, not head, friends. The text has her standing behind Him at His feet.

The answer is True. The Pharisee says to himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him…” (Luke 7:39). He never says it out loud. It's all happening inside his head.
The answer is True. The Pharisee only said it to himself, but the text says Jesus answered him (Luke 7:40). It doesn't say how Jesus knew. It just says He spoke up, and Simon heard it.
The answer is False. Simon says, “Tell me, Teacher…” (Luke 7:40). He asks to hear what Jesus has to say. Whatever was running through his head a minute ago, he leans in.
The answer is fifty. One man owed five hundred denarii and the other fifty (Luke 7:41). Two debts, and a big gap between them. Hold on to that gap, friends, because Jesus is about to use it.

The answer is False. When the two men were unable to repay, the text says “…he forgave both of them.” (Luke 7:42). The man with the smaller debt and the man with the bigger debt both walk away forgiven. That's the setup for the question coming next.

The answer is the one who was forgiven more. Simon says, “I suppose the one who was forgiven more…” (Luke 7:43). Listen to that little “I suppose.” I think he can feel something coming and wants to answer carefully.
The answer is True. Jesus tells him, “You have judged correctly…” (Luke 7:43). Simon gets the answer right. Keep an eye on where Jesus takes it from here, friends.

The answer is water for His feet. Jesus says, “When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.” (Luke 7:44). Water for the feet is the first thing on His list. The woman's tears do what the water didn't.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.” (Luke 7:45). Simon did not greet Him with a kiss. The woman has not stopped kissing His feet.

The answers are head and feet. Jesus says, “You did not anoint My head with oil…” (Luke 7:46). That's what Simon didn't do. Then He says “…but she has anointed My feet with perfume.” (Luke 7:46). Head for Simon's missing oil, feet for her perfume, friends.

The answer is that she has loved much. Jesus says, “…her many sins have been forgiven, for she has loved much.” (Luke 7:47). It lines up with the story of the two debtors, where the one forgiven more was the one who would love more. Jesus ties her story right back to it.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…he who has been forgiven little loves little.” (Luke 7:47). It's the other half of what He says about the woman. Same story of the two debtors, now pointed right at Simon's table.

The answer is “Who is this who even forgives sins?” (Luke 7:49). Those at the table begin to say it to themselves right after Jesus tells the woman her sins are forgiven. The text doesn't say what they decide.

The answer is True. The text says that as Jesus travels from town to town, “The Twelve were with Him…” (Luke 8:1). He's preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God, and they're right there with Him. That's a full road trip, friends.
The answer is seven. The text says “Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out…” (Luke 8:2). She's named as one of the women who had been healed. Quite a story behind that name.

The answer is that they are providing for them from their own resources. The text says, “These women were ministering to them out of their own means.” (Luke 8:3). Joanna, Susanna and many others were helping with what they had, friends.
